title: FitnessAnalysis Life Event
description: Human-provided context (health, life events, equipment changes, training decisions, etc.) used to augment analysis of the activity data. Not derived from any device, platform, or export -- entered by the user to explain patterns the raw data can't explain on its own.

id.description: Stable kebab-case slug identifying this event, e.g. 'back-injury-onset'. Referenced by other events via related_event_ids, so avoid changing it once set.

date.description: Start date (or the only date, for a point-in-time event), ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD). If only a month or year is known, use the 1st of that month/January 1st and set date_precision to 'approximate'.

date_precision.description: Whether `date` (and `date_end`, if present) is known precisely or is an approximation/best guess.

date_end.description: End date for a range/period event (e.g. a period of pain, a training block). Omit or null for a point-in-time event.

ongoing.description: True if this event/state began at `date` and was still true as of when this record was last updated, with no known end date yet.

category.description: Broad category for filtering. Extend this enum as new kinds of context come up.

title.description: Short human-readable label, e.g. for a chart annotation or list view.

description.description: Fuller narrative context, in the user's own words where possible -- this is where detail belongs, not just the title.

related_event_ids.description: IDs of other events in life_events.json that this one is causally or narratively linked to (e.g. a treatment event linking back to the diagnosis it followed).

recorded_at.description: When this entry was added to the file (provenance -- when it was recorded, not the event's own date).
